page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 64-bit ARM architecture. The system provides 96 physical cores across 96 dedicated vCPUs utilizing the ARMv9 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, with a single-thread per core design. Cache layout includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory provisioning reaches 768.0 GB of RAM, equating to an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance features a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no local bundled storage, and provides no discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional parallel execution and memory bandwidth. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (163,430.41), Geekbench multi-core performance (25,967.0), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (935.6 GB/sec), and Clang compilation (93,603.0). Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 481.61 GB/sec alongside 242.72 GB/sec of write bandwidth, driving top-decile scores in PassMark database operations (47,906.68) and Redis SET throughput (198.49 million operations/sec). In contrast, single-threaded metrics reflect average performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,895.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,705.89.

From an efficiency standpoint, the high memory density and 96 dedicated ARMv9 cores provide notable resource consolidation capabilities without hyperthreading contention. Tradeoffs include the total absence of local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures, and lower single-threaded throughput relative to its multi-core capabilities. The platform is well-matched for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-throughput static web serving, real-time analytics, and medium-to-large CPU-based LLM text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by 96 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation. It features 768.0 GB of memory (8.0 GB per core), 200 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth, no local ephemeral storage, and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded processing and memory throughput, scoring 163,430.41 in stress-ng multi-core tests, 481.61 GB/sec in uncached memory reads, and 198.49 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Single-threaded metrics, including a 1,895.0 Geekbench single-core score, fall into the median range. Without hyperthreading overhead, the instance delivers predictable execution efficiency across high-concurrency environments, making it suitable for distributed in-memory databases, Redis deployments, data caching layers, real-time analytics engines, and large-scale compilation workloads.
